_comment: Wilson's disease is the SANITY-CHECK case for the custom-node pipeline: unlike the other 3 diseases here, it already has approved treatments, so it should end up with real Compound-treats-Disease edges after merge.

node.name: Wilson's disease
node.notes: Autosomal recessive disorder of copper metabolism causing hepatic and neuropsychiatric copper toxicosis. Not present in Hetionet v1.0's 137-disease set.

supporting_nodes.name: ATP7B
supporting_nodes.notes: Copper-transporting P-type ATPase (ATPase copper transporting beta), chromosome 13q14.3. NCBI Gene ID 540. The sole gene causally associated with Wilson's disease.

supporting_nodes.name: Penicillamine
supporting_nodes.notes: Already present in Hetionet v1.0 as Compound::DB00859, not previously linked to Wilson's disease. Copper-chelating agent; first-line therapy since the 1950s-60s.

supporting_nodes.name: Trientine
supporting_nodes.notes: Triethylenetetramine (brand names Syprine, Cuvrior). Not present in Hetionet v1.0's compound set. Copper chelator, alternative to penicillamine for patients intolerant of it. DrugBank ID (approx.): DB06824 - not used as the node ID here since it is not verified against Hetionet's own DrugBank vocabulary snapshot.

supporting_nodes.name: Zinc acetate
supporting_nodes.notes: Brand name Galzin (US) / Wilzin (EU), FDA-approved 1997. Not present in Hetionet v1.0's compound set. Blocks intestinal copper absorption via metallothionein induction; used for maintenance therapy and in pre-symptomatic/pregnant patients.

edges.evidence: ATP7B loss-of-function variants are the established monogenic cause of Wilson's disease (OMIM #277900).
Penicillamine is FDA-approved and first-line copper-chelation therapy for Wilson's disease.
Trientine is FDA-approved copper-chelation therapy for Wilson's disease, typically second-line to penicillamine.
Zinc acetate (Galzin) is FDA-approved for maintenance therapy of Wilson's disease.
